Oral Answers      [3 DEC 2007]               to Question 3  
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sir, with regard to the q uantitative expansion 
education sector, when it comes to elementary education, expecting a considerable please 
in the allocation for education sector, we are look ing at rapid upgradation of about upper 
primary schools into secondary school  level and al so expand the of 44,000 existing 
secondary schools. Similarly, we are also-looking a t establishing ,000 quality model 
schools at the block level to serve as benchmarks o f excellence in secondary education. 
We are also looking at strengthening the provisions  for library and laboratt facilities in 
the existing schools and provide hostels and reside ntial schools, particularly for the girl 
children. On the Mid Day Meal Scheme, Sir, we are l ooking at expanding it fin to the 
3,479 educationally backward blocks so that the chi ldren in the upper elementary section 
are also covered. Through this, we are looking at b ringing almost 30 million children into 
the fold of the Mid Day Meal Scheme. When it comes to higher education, we have already 
said, time and again, that we are looking at increa sing the number of UTs, II NITs, etc. 
Definitely, Sir, we are looking at quantity as well as quality improvements. 
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: Hon. Chairman, Sir, without meaning any disrespect 
to the hon. Minister of State, in view of the impor tance of the question, we would have 
appreciated if the hon. Minister would have been he re. I am saying so because there is a 
distinct context of this query. The Hon. Minister h as just admitted that they are 
increasing the allocation in the Eleventh Plan. That is a welcome development. 'Education 
for All' is our common concern. But, Madam Minister, what is the report card? The sterling 
eloquence has come from the latest UNESCO Report, 6th Edition, where we regret to say, 'In 
the Report on Education for All Monitoring Report, India has dipped five points below 
from 100 India today is under bracket with Pakistan, with other smaller countries'. This is a 
matter of great concern which, at once, emphasises that delivery system is very poor. Today, 
we need to take a serious notice of the fact that o ut of total children who are out of 
schools 66 cent are girl child. The drop out rate i s growing faster and faster at 14.6 per 
cent. These are areas of eloquent serious concern w hich we need to take notice of. You 
may increase the Plan allocation; you have just sta ted that. My specific query, Madam 
Minister, (a) What special efforts are being made t o ensure that delivery of this huge 
quantum of money is properly implemented at the national level and the State level; and (b) 
What is the core focus of the Eleventh Plan? If the  focus of the Tenth Plan was primary 
education, is the focus of the Eleventh Plan? 
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sir, I hope the hon. Member has also taken stock of 
the fact that UNESCO Report has also appreciated the efforts that India has been putting in 
to ensure that education is made accessible and als o equitable. And, of course, taking the 
demographic challenge of our country into consideration, we are doing our best and we are 
trying to ensure that quality and quantity are ensu red and accessibility is also provided to 
all the children. Sir, with regard to the focus of the eleventh Plan, we are looking at 
vocationalisation of education and we would like to  take this up in the mission mode to 
ensure that the children who are out of school and who do not have access to forma! 
education or rather do not want to get into the stream of formal education, are brought into 
the fold of vocationalisation of education. 
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: Madam, you did not speak about delivery system 
all. My first query was, what attempts are being made to ensue that delivery system becomes 
more effective? 

4    Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sorry, Sir. We already have a monitoring system in 
place and we are trying to strengthen all the existing monitoring systems, particularly, with 
reference to Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Mid Day Meal and also the UGC. We would be taking 
it up with all of them to ensure that the monitoring system is strengthened. 
DR. P.C. ALEXANDER: Sir, I also endorse what my esteemed friend just now mentioned 
that in view of the importance of this question, we  would have appreciated if the Cabinet 
Minister was present. But, at the same time, I wish to compliment the junior Minister. She 
always come very well prepared for the answers and we can never find fault with her 
answers. She is one of the most promising young Ministers in the present Cabinet. 
Sir, mention has been made about the increase in th e size of the Plan for education. My 
question is about the capacity of the educational institutions in all the three sectors, higher, 
secondary and primary, to spend the amount that has  been provided or that is going to be 
provided. We are adding about 300 colleges and 5 to  6 universities every year and in my 
judgement, most of them do not have the capacity to spend whatever little the Government 
is giving. Therefore, will the hon. Minister give a n assurance to the House that you are 
making adequate steps to gear up the capacity of th e institutions for spending the amount 
that is likely to be given to them by improving the quality of the staff, infrastructure etc. and 
by priority being given to research and various other steps? 
Will the hon. Minister take into account these thin gs when he gives the answer to the 
question about capacity? Will the Ministry seriousl y consider splitting up the universities 
which are now existing? Some of the universities are having 400 to 500 affiliated colleges. 
Split up the universities so that every 3 or 4 district will have a university of their own, and 
accept the recommendations of the Knowledge Commission to have 50 model universities 
covering all over States all over the regions will the hon. Minister give an assurance that 
these recommendations will be carried out? 
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sir, even as I would like to thank my senior colleague 
for having complimented me, I don't think if the ho n. Human Resource Minister is not 
present here, it would mean that there would be a divergence in the policy that we would be 
stating here. Anyway, as per the capacity, the quarterly target for expenditure in the Ministry 
of Human Resource Development with reference to Dep artment of School Education and 
Literacy is required to spend about 50 per cent of its allocations by September, and 
Department of Higher Education was required to spend 42 per cent of its allocation, Sir, and 
even as the Department of Higher Education has alre ady spent close to 42 per cent, a little 
over 41 per cent, it is a matter of concern that school education and literacy has not actually 
reached the target of 50 per cent, and is hovering around a little over 31 per cent. The reason 
for this is the change in the sharing pattern of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. The three main 
schemes are, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Mid-day Meal and Adult Liter acy. There was a 
change in the sharing pattern between the Union Gov ernment and the State Governments 
with reference to Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan. Earlier, the ratio was 75:25, and it was changed to 
50:50, and because of the little confusion over the  sharing pattern, the pace of expenditure 
in Sarva Shiksha Abiyan was affected slightly. With reference to Mid-day Me al scheme, a 
decision was taken to extend the Mid-day Meal scheme to the upper primary classes. So, in 
view of that, there was a slight delay in the take off. With reference to the Adult Literacy 
scheme, because the plan had to be approved, there was a slight delay in the beginning of 
the adult education programme. But, however, since now it has come through, I am sure we 
would be able to achieve the target. 

Oral Answers  [3 DEC. 2007]  to Questions   5 
The other part of the question was about higher edu cation. In higher education, we are 
looking at strengthening library and the laboratory facilities, as I have mentioned earlier. We 
are also looking at expanding the number of UTs, II Ms, ITs and all that. So, capacity is 
definitely there to absorb the allocation there, an d I can assure the hon. Member that it 
would be qualitative absorption of all the allocations. 
DR. KARAN SINGH: Mr. Chairman, Sir, before I ask my question, I have a submission. 
What we really need is a full day structured debate on education because there are so many 
aspects to education, from the primary level all the way up, and so many different problems 
are there. We cannot get the necessary information just by asking odd questions, although 
the Minister reply is perfectly all right. Sir, maybe, if not in this Session, in the next Session, 
one whole day should be kept, at least, for a debat e. Sir, I travel around the country. 
Yesterday, I was in Mumbai and Pune, and whenever I  meet the press people, I make 
inquiries about th Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, and my feedback for what it is worth, is not very 
favourable. It is not a question of expenditure. Th e monies that are allotted, either are not 
spent or not spent properly. Unless you involve the  Panchayati Raj institutions from the 
Zila Parishad level down to the village level, you will not be able to ensure this. We sanction 
money. We have increased five-fold the expenditure on education. But how do you know 
that that money actually is getting spent? The monitoring cannot be done by the Government 
of India. It has to be done by the State Government through the Panchayati Raj institutions, 
and unless these institutions are involved, we will  never be able to get proper results. So, 
my question is, whether along with these very welcome enhanced allocations for education, 
are you also seriously thinking of modalities and mechanism for proper monitoring. 
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sir, there are already me chanisms in place for 
monitoring, like we have the MIS. Then, we have reg ular reviews conducted by the 
secretaries, and the hon. HRD Minister takes reviews with the State Governments also. 
With regard to expenditure, it is also the responsi bility of the State Governments to 
ensure that there is qualitative spending of allocations made by the Union Government. So, 
it is shared responsibility and we expect the State also to shoulder the responsibility. 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: Sir, a report contained in "The Global Digest, 2007" 
released by the UNESCO's Institute for Statistics s ays, "Households pay more than one-
quarter, 28 per cent, of the costs to send their ch ildren to primary and secondary school". 
"Yet, at the same time, the households assume just 14 per cent of the costs for university 
education", it added in that report. Sir, when utmost priority should be given to education— 
we talk about primary education, education for all and universal primary education—the 
comparable cost of education between primary, secon dary and university education, as 
revealed in the report, is high. My question is: Wh at is the reaction of the Government to 
this report? This is my question to the Minister. 
SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI: Sir, as far as public schools are concerned, education 
under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, as we all are aware, is compulsory and free also. I think, the 
28 per cent that the hon. Member is talking about could be for the private school education. 
But as far as Government schools are concerned, education is free. 
With reference to higher education, CABE Committee has recommended that the resources 
that could be collected through fee should meet up to 20 per cent of the recurring expenses 
so that education is actually accessible to everybody; whereas we do have a recommendation 
from the National Knowledge Commission which says that the resources that could be

Pooled from the fee should meet, at least, 20 per cent. But realising that the accessibility is 
important, there is still a debate on whether the f ee should be high or whether it should 
whatever level it is. But accessibility has always been a priority with the lndia.

† *242. DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD:†† 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) Wheter it is a fact that Government has formula ted a scheme to charge the bill 
amount for electricity consumption from the rural c onsumers in the country by paying 
ion to non-Government institutions to charge the same; 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi.  
†† The question was acasked on the floor of the House by Shri Ravi Shankar Prasad. 

Oral Answers  [ 3  DEC. 2007]  to Questions   7 
(b) if so, the details of the said scheme; 
(c) whether this scheme is already in force in certain States, if so, the names of such 
States; and 
(d) what are the likely benefits of implementing this scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) to (d): A Statement is 
laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) Section 14 proviso (vii) of Electricity Act 2003, provides for appointment of franchisees 
by distribution licensees to undertake distribution on their behalf. 
(b) Various models for appointment of franchisees are being followed by utilities, ranging 
from revenue based franchisee (for undertaking mete ring, billing and collection) to input 
based franchisee (responsible for revenue collectio n, operation and maintenance and 
improvement of service to consumers). 
(c) 14 States have reported appointment of franchis ees, namely, Uttarakhand, Uttar 
Pradesh, West Bengal, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, 
Bihar, Orissa, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Assam, Nagaland in rural areas. 
(d) The likely benefits of the franchisee system to the power sector are: 
(0 Improvement in consumer services; 
(ii) Enhancement in revenue collection; 
(iii) Reduction in Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses; and (iv) 
Development of productive loads of agriculture and rural industry for better revenue 
substainability of rural electrification, etc.

Increase in number of old age homes 
† * 244. SHRIMATI PREMACARIAPPA: Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry has any proposal/scheme to inc rease the number of old age 
homes in different parts of the country, specially in Karnataka; 
(b) if so, the details of funds sanctioned for the same and by when the scheme is going 
to be implemented; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SMT . MEIRA 
KUMAR): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House, (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. During 
the 10th Plan period, the actual expenditure on the  schemes being implemented by the 
Ministry for Senior Citizens was Rs. 77.34 crore. T he Working Group constituted by the 
Planning Commission have recommended a provision of Rs. 265 crore during the 11 th Plan 
period. With the proposed increase, in the budget, the consequential benefits will flow 
down to the deserving senior citizens in the country, including Karnataka. 
SHRIMATI PREMACARIAPPA: Sir, there are hundreds of old-age homes in the country 
and also many in Karnataka. I would like to know from the hon. Minister as to how many 
old-age homes are functioning properly and whether there is any monitoring cell to review 
the functioning of the on-going projects of old-age homes. 
SHRIMATI MEIRA KUMAR: Sir, at the moment, we have 437 old-age homes all over the 
country, and we have a definite system of monitorin g. The officers of the ministry go on 
inspection tour to check their functioning, and als o the State Governments send their 
officers for inspection. We receive reports from the NGOs which are maintaining and running 
these old-age homes. We receive half-yearly reports and yearly reports from them. In fact, 
on the basis of these reports which we receive, we give them further grant-in-aid. So, on the 
basis of all this monitoring that is being done, I can assure the hon. Member that the old-age 
homes that are being maintained through the grant-i n-aid given by the Ministry are 
functioning well. 
SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA: Sir, there is a provision of Rs. 265 crores in the Eleventh 
Plan which is three times more than the provision of the Tenth Plan. Sir. I would like to know

from the hon. Minister about the various facilities being given to the senior citizens in the 
old-age homes and how many old-age homes are going to be estabilished in the Eleventh 
plan. I would also like to know from the hon. Minister whether the Ministry is planning to 
merge these old-age homes with the children homes s o that it will be good for the senior 
citizens to be with children. 
SHRIMATI MEIRA KUMAR: Sir, we are in the process of  revising the Integrated 
programme for Older Persons. One of the objectives of it is to run old-age homes. We are in 
the process of increasing the maintenance allowance and other expenditure. We are linking 
it to the price index. Apart from that, we are goin g to give other facilities. We are in the 
process of revising it, which will naturally enhance the cost per old-age home. As far as the 
suggestion of the hon. Member to merge the children  homes with the old-age homes is 
concerned, that, certainly, seems to be a very good  suggestion. However, the functioning 
of the two is the responsibility of two different M inistries. So, I don't know how far that 
would be feasible. But, I would like to inform the House, through you, Sir, that we lay a great 
deal of emphasis on inter-generational relationship that the children should be encouraged 
to care for the elderly people. We want to emphasis e it, and we have several programmes 
running for that. 
DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A. HEPTULLA: Sir, the hon. Minister for Child Development 
is also sitting there. 
SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI:  Sir, the question of elderly people in our country is becoming 
serious day-by-day. Sir, the culture of our country had been to look after the parents in their 
old age. But, unfortunately, this culture is changi ng. Sir, in Andhra Pradesh as well as in 
Maharashtra, a Bill has been passed making it compulsory for the children to look after their 
parents. I would like to know from the hon. Ministe r whether the Central Government is 
considering bringing this type of a Bill in the whole of the country also so as to make living 
comfortable for parents of all children. This is part (a) of my question. 
Part (b) of the question is, Sir, it is true that in the State of Maharashtra, the Government 
does not run old-age homes. They are being looked a fter by the private people, by some 
social organisations. The Government gives them the land free of charge to construct, also 
the Government gives them sufficient grant for the people who are working in old-age 
homes and thereafter this becomes more convenient f or the people. I would like to know 
whether the Government would also like to adopt the  same system in the whole of the 
country. 
SHRIMATI MEIRA KUMAR: Sir, so far as the Bill is concerned, I share the concern of 
the hon. Member about the disintegration of the joint family system and the marginalisation 
and neglect of the elderly in our society where they were always treated with great reverence 
and respect. However, considering the new realities , we have formulated a Bill for the 
maintenance and welfare of parents and the older pe rsons which was introduced in the 
lower House and which was subsequently sent to the Standing Committee of the Ministry 
and they have given their report. Based on the report, it has been cleared by the Cabinet and 
further action will be taken. It is in the process. I hope, once it has been enacted, it will take 
care of the elderly, their protection, their securi ty, their health-care, their maintenance not 
only the elderly, because elderly are 60-plus but also of parents. Mother and father may not 
be 60-plus but if they have not source of income an d if they are not able to take care of 
themselves, even when they are below 60, the adult children who are economically self-
reliant have to take care of them. We are bringing it all in this Bill.

The other part of the question was that we should d o what the State Government of 
Maharashtra is doing. But we are already doing this. This is how we are running the old-age 
homes. We are giving funds to the NGOs, to the panc hayati-raj institutions, to voluntary 
organisations, to self-help groups to cosntruct old -age homes. But the land has to be 
provided by them. But, now we are in the process of revising this scheme where we would 
enhance our share. In all probability, we might even give them a hundred per cent. In other

Performance of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan 
†*245. SHR KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of HUMA N RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is satisfied with the performance of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan; 
(b) whether Government is aware of the poor allocation for this Scheme; and 
(c) if so,  the steps taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (c) The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has been progressing satisfactorily, particularly 
in reducing the number of out of school children in the 6-14 years age group from 3.20 crore 
in 2001-02 to about 75 lakhs in 2007 and augmenting  school infrastructure wherein inter 
alia 1.18 lakh school buildings, 4.05 lakh additional classrooms have been constructed and 
7.95 lakh teachers recruited by 31.3.2007. 
To continue the momentum in the programme, an allocation of Rs. 10671 crore has been 
made in the Central Government's budget for the year 2007-08 and the Centre-State funding 
pattern for the Xlth Plan period has been modified in the raio of 65:35 for the year 2007-08 & 
2008-09, gradually tapering off to a 50:50 ratio in the last year of the Xlth Plan for all States 
except the North Eastern (NE) States, where for the latter the sharing pattern will be 90:10, 
with the Central Government's share being resourced from the 10% earmarked funds for the 
NE States under SSA's Central Government budget.

Specific Programme to Check Dropouts  
*248.  SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that there has been an increase in the number of 
dropouts from elementary school during the current year; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether there is any specific programme planned by Government to reduce the 
number during the current Plan period; and 
(d) if so, the details of the programme and the ratio of Central allocation for this programme, 
State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): (a) 
to (d) The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a nationa l programme being implemented in 
partnership with the States, in which, inter alia, one of the goals specifies retention of all 
children upto the elementary level by 2010. The dro pout rate has fallen sharply by 11.3 
percentage points at primary level since 2001 upto 2004, compared to a decline of only 2.3 
percentage points between the years 1990 to 2000. The dropout rate at the elementary level 
declined from 53.7% in 2000-01 to 50.84% in 2004-05. 
A multi-pronged approach has been adopted under the SSA for reducing dropout rates. 
These include, inter alia, strengthening of schools and improving the quality of education 
through improvement in school infrastructure, recruitment of additional teachers, provision 
of annual school grants, regular training of teache rs, regular academic support to teachers 
etc. In addition, interventions under SSA also aim at building community support, flexible 
schooling for the hardest to reach children, specia l provisions to promote education of 
girls, as well as children with special needs. The Mid-day-Meal programme also complements 
the strategy to reduce dropout rates. 
The Central-State funding pattern for the Xlth Plan period is in the ratio of 65:35 for the 
first two years, 60:40 in the third year, 55:45 in the fourth and 50:50 in the final year of the 
Plan period for all States/UTs except the North Eastern States where it will be in the ratio of 
90:10 with the Central Share being resourced from the 10% earmaked funds for the region in 
SSA's central budget.

(b) the areas of education that are to be offered by such univerisites; 
 
(c) whether there would be a mechanism to oversee the a ctivities of the foreign 
universities; and 
(d) whether Government would permit 'fly by night' operators from abroad to come and 
set up their shops in the name of offering higher education and is aware of its full implications?

THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): (a) 
to (d) At present, only the All India Council for T echnical Education (AICTE) has framed 
regulations, which were last revised in the year 2005, for the entry and operation of foreign 
universities/institutions for imparting technical e ducation in India. A legislative proposal 
for regulating the entry and operation of foreign e ducational institutions, seeking, among 
other things, prevention of the entry of sub-standa rd educational institutions, is under 
consideration of the  Government. 
Academic Imbalance in some regions 
† *250. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH: Will the Minister o f HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to th ose regions of the country 
where for want of basic and technical educational i nstitutions, students are being deprived 
of proper education - 
(b) if;so, details of the  regions where technical institutions are not availa ble till now, 
State-wise; and  
(c) the measures being taken by Government to overcome academic imbalance in those 
regions? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): (a) to 
(c) In order to ensure that students are not deprived of basic education, the Government has 
put in place the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) for Un iversalisation of Elementary 
education in the country. 
According to the information furnished by the All India Council for Technical Education 
(AICTE), the Union Territories (UT) of Andaman and Nicobar, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, 
Dadra & Nagar Haveli and the State of Nagaland, do not have an AICTE approved degree 
level technical institution. The UT of Lakshadweep does not have an AICTE approved 
diploma level techical institution. The AICTE which accords approval for the Establishment 
of new technical institutions does not have any pro posals from these UTs/State for setting 
up of new technical institutions. 
In order to mitigate the regional disparities in te chnical education, the Government has 
made provisions for reservation of seats in degree and diploma level technical courses for 
States/UTs lacking such facilities in other States/ UTs where such technical education 
facilities are available. The existing polytechnics  in Andaman and Nicobar and Nagaland 
were supported through a World Bank assisted project called the Third Technician Education 
Project for capacity expansion, quality enhancement and efficiency improvement. In the XI 
Plan, it is proposed to have a Central University in each of the 16 States which at present do 
not have a Central University.

*251. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Assam accounts for around 48 per cent of the women trafficked 
out from the North-Eastern Region;

(b) if so, the details thereof, alongwith the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the action plan of Government to address this menace? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) As per information 
received from Assam State Government, there are reports about women from Assam being 
trafficked outside the State and rescued by appropr iate authorities. The reasons indicated 
are poverty, lack of education, unemployment, unhealthy social living condition, etc. 
(c) The State Government has informed that apart from appropriate intervention taken up 
by the Police Department for prevention and control of trafficking in women and girl children 
the Social Welfare Department has introduced an Act ion Plan to set up State Homes for 
Women rescued from moral danger, training and rehabilitation package through schemes of 
Swayamsida, promotional NGO action in creating awareness on the evil effects of trafficking. 
The Ministry of Women and Child Development, Govern ment of India also conducts 
advocacy, awareness generation, sensitization progr ammes for prevention of trafficking. 
The Ministry runs Swadhar Shelter Homes, which provide shelter, food, clothing, emotional 
support, counseling, rehabilitation and other facilities to victims of trafficking. The Immoral 
Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA) supplemented by the Indian Penal Code prohibits 
trafficking in human beings for purpose of prostitu tion and lays down severe penalties for 
traffickers.

(ii) 50% books should be purchased in Hindi. 
(iii) Judgments in the courts of the States should be delivered in Hindi and entrance

(v) Language of the Administrative Tribunals should be Hindi instead of English and the 
meetings of Hindi Salahakar Samiti should be convened twice or thrice a year. 
(c) The following action has been taken to implement the suggestions: 
(i) Correspondence in bilingual form is being done as per the directions issued by Rajbhasha 
Vibhag and process of filling the vacant posts in Hindi side is under way in the Department. 
(ii) Action is being taken to purchase books in Hindi as per the norms fixed for it. 
(iii) Article 348 (1) (a) provides that, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, all the 
proceedings in Supreme Court and every High court shall be in English language. Under 
Article 348 (2), the Governor of a State may, with the previous consent of the President, 
authorize the use of the Hindi language or any other language used in for any official 
purposes of the State, in proceedings in the High Court having its principal seat in that 
State. Four States i.e. Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan have started 
using Hindi in the proceedings of High Court. 
So far as conducting of entrance examination for LL.B is concerned, no combined entrance 
examination for LL.B is conducted at present. Although, a demand was made for holding 
combined Entrance Examination in the case (Varum Bhagat Vs Union of India and others) 
before Supreme Court, in regard to which, as per the directions of Hon'ble Supreme Court, 
efforts are being made to evolve consensus among the National Law Universities located 
in various States. At present, every University is at liberty to conduct entrance examination 
for LL.B Course and the entrance examination of LL.B is conducted like entrance 
examination of other subjects in that language in which courses/medium of the concerned 
University are prescribed. Ministry of Human Resource and Development can advise, on 
behalf of the Central Govt., the Central Universiti es including other Universities in 
this regard, however, prescribing the medium of entrance examination ultimately depends 
on the concerned University. The suggestion given by the Committee is being referred 
to Central Universities and other Universities thro ugh University Grants 
Commission. 
(iv)   Under article 348 (2) of the Constitution until Parliament by law otherwise provides, 
legislative drafting cannot be done in Hindi language. Most of the advocates are allowed to 
argue proceedings in Hindi at District Level Courts and the work is being done in Hindi 
therein. 
(v)   Administrative Tribunals do not fall within the jurisdiction of Ministry of Law and Justice. 
(vi)  On two occasions, the dates for holding the meeting of the Hindi Salahakar Samiti were 
fixed but due to unavoidable circumstances, it could not be held. The next meeting is to be 
decided after the current Parliament Session.

1347.  SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESO URCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that black marketing of foodgr ains, meant for distribution to 
children in Government schools under the Mid Day Meal Scheme, have been seized by the 
police in the recent past, which were allegedly provided to them by certain non-government 
organizations (NGOs), and such practice is on rampant; and 
(b) the measures Government proposes to put a check on improper use of the food 
materials by the NGOs? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) Some cases of blackmarketing and misuse of foodgrain 
meant for Mid Day Meal Scheme have come to the noti ce of the Government. Details and 
action taken are given the Statement. (See below) 
(b) The Mid Day Meal guidelines provide for associa tion of voluntary agencies in the 
supply of cooked mid day meal. The identification o f voluntary agencies is made at the 
State/district level. The following aspects are required to be taken into consideration while 
determining the suitability of a voluntary agency for supply of cooked mid day meal. 
(i) The voluntary agency should not discriminate in  any manner on the basis of 
religion, caste and creed, and should not use the p rogramme for propagation of 
any religious practice. 
(ii) The voluntary agency should be a body that is registered under the Societies 
Registration Act or the Public Trust Act, and should have been in existence for a 
minimum period of two years. 
(iii) There should be a commitment to undertake sup ply responsibility on a no-profit 
basis. 
(iv) It should have financial and logistic capacity  to supply the mid day meal on the 
requisite scale. 
(v) It should abide by the parameters of the mid da y meal scheme particularly with 
regard to the prescription of eligible children, nutrition content etc. 
(vi) It should be willing to work with PRIs/Municipal bodies in accordance with relevant 
guidelines of the State Government. 
(vii) It should furnish to the body assigning the work to it an Annual Report along with 
audited statement of accounts in terms of all grant s received from the State 
Government, both in cash and kind, duly certified b y an approved Chartered 
Account-it. 
(viii) The voluntary organization shall not entrust sub-contract the programme or divert 
any part of the assistance (food grains / money) to any other organization/agency.

(ix) It should give a commitment to return to the State Government any permanent semi permanent 
assets, acquired by the Voluntary Organization from the grants received under programme, 
once it ceases to undertake the supply work.  
(x) All accounts, stock and registers maintained by the voluntary organization should be open 
to inspection by officers appointed by the State Government.  
(xi) State Government may prescribe such other conditions, as they may deem appropriate

Inclusion of solid waste management in school curriculum 
1353. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Ministry of Urban Development has approached in Ministry of HRD, to 
include solid waste management in school curriculum to sensitise the younger generations 
to manage municipal waste in a hygienic and scientific manner; and 
(b) if so, whether Government is thinking of taking  a holistic view so that younger 
generations have wider exposure to environmental ha zards, though it may be an isolated 
attempt to encourage the principle of reduce, reuse and recycle? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) Concepts of waste management have already been incorporated in the school 
curriculum prepared by National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT). 
Class XII Geography textbook deals with 'Environmen tal Pollution' and 'Urban Waste 
Disposal". Similarly, textbooks for Classes VI, VII, X and XI contain Chapters on the subjects 
such as 'Garbage in Garbage out', 'Managing the Garbage We Produce', etc. 
Primary school without buildings 
†  1354.    SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:  
SHRI SURENDRA LATH:  
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of primary schools operating without a building till now, State-wise; 
(b) the steps taken by Government for construction of b uildings for these schools 
during the last three years; 
(c) whether any policy has been formulated by Government for the promotion of primary 
education in States; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) As per data base of District Information System for 
Education (D1SE) collected and analysed by the National University for Educational Planning 
and Administration for the year 2006-07,26551 Government primary schools did not have 
buildings. The State-wise details are at Statement-I (See below). These are largely on account 
of new schools opened/notified by State Govts., but  where the construction of school 
buildings is still to be completed, at the time of annual D1SE data collection. 
(b) Under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan programme, during the last three years, i.e. 2004-
05,2005-06 and 2006-07, a total number of 23901,25024 and 42219 primary school buildings 
have been sanctioned respectively. The State-wise d etails for last three years are at 
Statement II (See below). 
(c) and (d) The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan programme to universalize elementary education 
in a time bound manner is being implemented in partnership with the States.

Findings about age of nursery students  
1355. SHRIMATI MOHSINA KIDWAI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a) whether Government is aware of the study conducted by Researchers from Oxford 
University and the Institute of Fiscal Studies, wherein it has been stated that children under 
three and a half years of age attending nursery classes, are likely to become upset and also 
display anti-social behaviour; and 
(b) if so, whether this Study coupled with recent suggestions of Ganguly Committee, 
banning admission of below 37 2 years children, become benchmark, resulting in gradual 
closure of play schools, etc., where children of more than two years are very often admitted? 
THE MI NI S TER OF S TATE I N THE MI NI S TR Y OF HUMAN RES OUR CE DEVEL OP MENT  
(SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) and (b) The Government is not aware of the study 
conducted by Researcher from Oxford University and the Institute of Fiscal Studies. However, 
as per information furnished by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and 
National Council for Educational Research and Training (NCERT), early introduction to a 
formal curriculum may increase anxiety and have a negative impact on children's self esteem 
and motivation to learn. The Ganguly Committee, in its report on Pre-Primary and Pre-
school Education in Delhi submitted to the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, observed and 
recommended that pre-school education should be for one year and the age should be four 
plus as on 31st March of the year of admission to pre-primary class.

Utilization of information of GSI and IBM 
1386. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the information provided by the Geological Survey of India and the Indian 
Bureau of Mines is not fully utilized; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the action taken to ensure full utilization thereof? 
THE MTNISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF MINES (DR T. SUBBARAMI REDDY): 
(a) to (c) Geological Survey of India (GSI) carries out regional mineral exploration including 
exploration for coal and investigations of societal  needs (e.g. earthquake, landslides, 
environment, engineering geology etc.). GSI generates information on airborne geophysical 
anomaly analog maps-namely, magnetic, electromagnetic and spectrometric (Potassium, 
Thorium, Uranium and Total Count). The Coal Wing of GSI produce geological reports for 
regional exploration of coal, lignite and coal bed methane (CBM) in the coalfields located in 
different parts of the country. Customized data packages and geological reports are also 
prepared by Coal Wing to aid in allotment of the blocks/sectors to public/private bidders for 
CBM exploration. 
Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) is a national repository of varied types of information on 
mines and minerals in the country. IBM collects inf ormation on mining geology, ore 
beneficiation and environmental studies, preparing mineral maps with forest overlays and 
National Mineral Inventory of mineral resources. Th e same are provided to various 
Government agencies (at National, State and Distric t level), public sector undertakings, 
private entrepreneurs, research & development and educational institutions, mining industry 
and prospective entrepreneurs. 
With the enunciation of the National Mineral Policy in the year 1993, the mineral sector 
has been liberalised for private sector participation and the various reports and information 
available with the GSI and the IBM on mineral exploration are utilized both by private sector 
and Government agencies depending on the needs arising due to demand for any specific 
data. 
With a view to ensure easy accessibility to the dat a, GSI maintains a website i.e. 
www.gsi.gov.in, which provides salient information on maps, reports and publications. GSI 
has also launched its own Portal which has the capa bility to search for information on 
various aspects like geological information, nature and price of maps, publications, information 
on priced and unpublished reports, selected information on economic deposits. GSI reports 
are also made available to the concerned State Gove rnments or Central agencies with 
scientific evaluation of the subject and recommendations. The data maintained at IBM is 
available on sale at a nominal price.

Production of bio-diesel 
1402. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the efforts being made by Government for production of Bio-diesel in the country; 
(b) the progress made in this regard; 
(c) whether the target fixed for the purpose has been achieved; 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) the target fixed for the next financial year, State-wise. 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NE WAND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) and (b) The Government of India has given top priority 
for promotion and use of bio-fuels, which includes bio-diesel and bio-ethanol. Considering 
the importance of promotion and use of bio-fuels fo r transportation, stationary and other 
applications, the Government of India has issued a Notification in July, 2006 giving specific 
responsibilities to various Union Ministries and De partments. The Government emphasis 
use of non-edible oils such as Jatropha curcas, Pongamia pinnata oils, etc. for production of 
bio-diesel and use of forest & non-forest wasteland s for plantation of non-edible oil seed 
bearing plants. 
The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy has sponsored R&D projects on bio-fuels to 
some leading R&D Institutions. Process parameters for production of bio-diesel from Jatropha 
curcas (Ratanjot) and Pongamia pinnata (Karanja) have been optimized; field trials on diesel 
car have been carried out with different levels of blend of bio-diesel produced from Jatropha 
and Pongamia with diesel. The vehicle response has been found to be comparable with 
diesel vehicles. A200 liter capacity per batch bio-diesel reactor has been designed, fabricated 

118    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SAB HA]  Unstarred Questions  
and developed. The MNRE has prepared a Draft National Policy on Bio-fuels, which is under 
consideration of Government of India.  
The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) has provided financial support to nine States in 
2005-06 for raising of about 18 crore seedlings of Jatropha and Pongamia and to 18 States in 2006-07 
for raising of another about 18 crore seedlings of these plants. The proposal of the MoRD for 
establishment of the National Mission on Bio-diesel and launch of its demonstration phase (Phase-I) 
is under consideration of Government of India.  
Department of Bio-Technology has initiated a Micro-mission programme on production and 
demonstration of superior quality planting material of Jatropha based on oil content of 30-35% and 
seed yield of 3-5 tonnes per hectare. They have raised 22.48 lakh plants under nursery at different 
places and have initiated R&D projects for improvement of oil quality and seed yield and 
identification of superior varieties.  
The Ministry of Agriculture through National Oil Seeds and Vegetable Oils Development 
(NOVOD) Board is promoting Jatropha and Pongamia un der the Scheme of Integrated 
Development of Tree borne oil seeds. The NOVOD Board has undertaken model plantation of Jatropha 
in about 10,000 hectare area and Karanja in about 1400 hectare area for producing parent material for 
undertaking large scale plantation. NOVOD Board have identified elite planting material of Jatropha 
and Pongamia under their R&D programme and have preserved the germ plasm. Besides, NOVOD 
Board has sanctioned model plantation of Jatropha in 1445 hectare and Karanja in 55 hectare 
during 2007-08.  
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), under All India Coordinated Research Project 
(AICRP) on agro-forestry, have initiated efforts in respect of Jatropha for collection of germ plasm, 
evaluation trials for growth, seed yield and oil content, hybridization, reproductive biology, agri-
silvicultural trials, molecular characterization, biochemical activities and farmers training. ICAR 
has identified a Jatropha variety for commercial cultivation.  
(c) to (e) Presently, the activities initiated by the Government are concentrating on research & 
development for development of superior quality planting materials and bio-diesel production 
technologies, testing of diesel engines using bio-diesel and their demonstration, etc. Targets 
are, therefore, not fixed.

(a) whether it is a fact that Government has not adequa tely exploited the potential of 
wind power on the East Coast;

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) No, Sir. Wind surveys have been conducted in coastal 
areas including East Coast under the Wind Resource Assessment programme of the Ministry. 
39 sites which could be considered suitable for wind power development have been identified 
in East Coast. 
(b) No, Sir. 216 potential sites in 13 States/Union Ter ritories have been identified as

country, by providing fiscal incentives such as con cessional import duty on certain 
components of wind electricity generator, excise duty exemption, ten years tax holiday on 
income generated from wind power projects, benefit of accelerated depreciation and loan 
from Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA). Technical support including 
detailed wind resource assessment to identify furth er potential sites is provided by the 
Centre for Wind Energy Technology (C-WET). This apart, preferential tariff is being provided 
for wind power in most of the potential States.

Standardization of time schedule for completion of power projects  
1410. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN: 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any standardization of time schedule for construction of coal-based thermal 
power projects has been firmed up for 500 MW and above capacity plants; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether sixty four months have been given for commissioning of first unit of Mundra 
UMPP and eighty eight months for the last unit; and 
(e) if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) to (c) A committee 
consisting of members from Central Electricity Authority (CEA), National Thermal Power 
Corporation Limited, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, Maharashtra State Electricity Board 
and Andhra Pradesh State Electricity Board, recomme nded milestones for execution of 
thermal power projects with capacity of 210/250 and  500 MW units. Based on the 
recommendations of the Committee, it was conveyed to all the power utilities in July, 2000 
that the commercial operation of 500 MW units should be completed within 51 months from 
the date of placement of order for main plant equipment and its auxiliaries. 
Subsequently in the year 2006, during review for th e purpose of comprehensive award 
scheme of the Ministry of Power, reasonable time schedule for completion of the first unit of 
500 MW was kept as 44 months for the green field projects and 41 months for the extention 
projects with additional six months for subsequent units. 
There are no standard time schedules for units above 500 MW because no such project 
has been completed so far . 
(d) Yes, Sir. 
(e) The capacity of Mundra Ultra Mega Power Project is proposed as 5 units of 800 MW. 
The construction period for larger size units of 80 0 MW with supercritical technology is 
more than that required for 500 MW units. Further, the commissioning period of 64 months 
for the first unit and 88 months for the last unit in Mundra UMPP is from the date of signing 
of Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and these periods  include 12 months for financial 
closure. However, the developer has an option under the PPA to advance the commissioning 
schedule.

Hydro electric power potential  
1412.   PROF. P.J. KURIEN: 
SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATURVEDI: 
 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any survey has been conducted on the total hydro electric power potential 
in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c) the percentage already tapped, State-wise; 
(d) whether this exploitation is being done by projects under Government and private 
sectors, if so, in what quantity it is being done giving the details thereof, State-wise; 

134    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(e) the quantity of potential which remains unexploited and the reasons therefor; 
(f) whether Government has any action plan to tap the full potential; and 
(g) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The 
reassessment studies of hydro-electric potential of  the country, completed by the Central 
Electricity Authority in 1987, have placed the hydr o power potential at 1,48,701 MW in 
terms of installed capacity. 
As on 15.11.2007, 31,439.5 MW (21.14%) of the poten tial has been tapped and 14,177 
MW (9.53%) is under construction. The state-wise de tails of hydro potential developed, 
under construction, yet to be developed and percent age thereof in terms of installed 
capacity are given at Statement-I. 
(d) Yes, Sir. The State-wise break-up of potential developed in Central Sector, State 
Sector and Private Sector is given in Statement-II. 
(e) About,. 1,03,000 MW of the estimated potential remains untapped. The main reasons 
for slow pace of development of hydro-electric potential in the country are as under:— 
(0  Difficult/inaccessible sites 
(ii)  Inadequate infrastructural facilities 
(iii)  Environmental forest and wildlife clearance related problems 
(iv)  Land acquisition and rehabilitation problems 
(v)  Adverse geological conditions 
(vi)  Transmission/Evacuation constraints 
(vii)  Appointment of project cost among various beneficiaries 
(viii)  Law and order problems 
(ix)  Inter State issues. 
(f) and (g) The Government of India is committed to  the speedy development of hydro 
power in the country. However, the development of the entire potential will depend on the 
techno-economic viability of the projects, and the policies of the respective host State 
Governments to harness this potential.

Rural electrification programme 
1413. SHRI B.S. GNANADESIKAN: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has proposed to make rural electrification programme mandatory 
for States, manage rural electric distribution through Franchisees; 
(b) if so, to what extent this programme would be beneficial for those of the nearly 1.5 
lakh villages and 78 million rural households, which are still awaiting for electrification; 

140    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(c) whether Government would consider to treat the loca l Panchayats as franchisees to 
the fiscal promotion of local authority; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): (a) Yes, Sir. Deployment 
of franchisees for management of rural distribution in projects financed under Rajiv Gandhi 
Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY) has been made mandatory. The States have provided 
prior commitment for deployment of franchisees under RGGVY before sanction of the projects 
to avail capital subsidy under the scheme. 
(b) Deployment of franchisees in the rural distribution system would be beneficial to the 
rural Households and is likely to improve customer service, improve the revenue collection 
and reduce losses of the state power utilities. Bas ed on sample study by independent 
NGOs following benefits have already been felt as a  result of installation of franchisees 
system:— 
1. Generation of Business opportunities for the local people. 
2. Direct employment to villagers including women. 
3. Improvement in consumer services. 
4. Enhancement in revenue collection. 
5. Increase in domestic, commercial and agriculture consumers. 
6. Decrease in AT & C losses. 
7. Consumer records in villages have been systematized. 
8. Defective meter replacements are in process and electronic meters owned by 
consumers are in use. 
9. Regular meter reading and billing on monthly basis is in progress. 
(c) to (e) Under RGGVY, Panchayati Raj Institutions  will have an important role of 
overseeing, in advisory capacity, the delivery of s ervices by the franchisees according to 
their identified responsibilities. The State Government could also encourage the Panchayati 
Raj institutions to take on responsibility of franc hisee as and when such institutions have 
developed to the extent that they can undertake con tractual obligations, raise resources 
form market and can discharge associated legal resp onsibilities. In such cases, appropriate 
mechanisms should be put in place by the state gove rnment for independent overseeing of 
the franchisee function of these institutions.

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a ) and (b) The

projections and State Sector capacity addition prog ramme proposed for the 11th Plan, 
States were duly consulted. Furthermore, the State-wise capacity addition programme was 
discussed in the Conference of Chief Secretaries and Power Secretaries of States on 23rd & 
24th April, 2007 and in the Chief Ministers conference held on 28th May, 2007 in New Delhi, 
and in the Standing Group of Ministers meeting held on 24th September, 2007.

Improvment in power sector  
1416. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that the true potential of LT. revolution has not been realized in the country, 
owing to lack of adequate power generation and its poor distribution system, particularly in rural 
areas; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the measures contemplated to augment power generation and to 
streamline its distribution? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a ) According to 
information received from Department of Information and Technology, most Information 
Communication Technology (ICT) applications are fairly dependent on electricity and deficiency 
in supply of power to such applications will reduce the true potential of IT revolution in the rural 
areas. However, few Schemes related to ICT applications launched by Department of IT has taken note 
of the existing power situation in rural India and adequate provisions have been made in the Schemes 
to provide back-up power in the event of nonavailability of regular power during prime 
business hours.  
(b) To augment the supply of electricity in the country a capacity addition of 78,577 MW has been 
proposed in the XI Plan. To provide reliable and quality power supply to rural areas, the Rajiv 
Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana has been launched, and under the scheme it has inter-alia been 
envisaged that States must make adequate arrangements for supply of electricity, and there should be 
no discrimination in the hours of supply between rural and urban households.

(a) whether it is a fact that there is a slippage in power generation capacity during the current 
plan period; 
(b) if so, the reasons for the slow progress; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the current plan's target of power sector is nearly four times 
what was achieved during the Tenth Five Year Plan; 
(d) whether Government would expedite the project to avoid excessive cost variance by 
forwarding to the next Five Year Plan as it did during the current Plan; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof?

However, according to the present assessment, the expected capacity addition is likely to be 12039 
MW (Thermal: 9007 MW, Hydro: 2372 MW & Nuclear: 660 MW). The main reasons for slippages 
in power generation capacity during the first year of the plan, inter-alia include:  
• Delay in supplies/erection by suppliers/contractors 
• Deployment of inadequate manpower 
•   Non availability of gas

Increase in energy demand 
1418.   SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: 
SHRI DARA SINGH: 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Paris-based agency in its World Energy Outlook 2007 has reportedly said 
that India and China would account for around 45 per cent of the increase in global primary 
energy demand by 2030, when the world's energy needs are expected to be well over 50 per 
cent higher than they are today; and 
(b) if so, what steps Government proposes to take to curb our demand, green house gas 
emissions and shift in investment in favour of clea ner, more efficient and more secure 
energy technologies? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) Yes, Sir. World 
Energy Outlook in its 2007 edition has stated that China and India together account for 45% 
of the increase in global primary energy demand, and the energy use by both these countries 
is set to more than double between 2005 and 2030. The report further adds that the momentum 
of economic development looks set to keep energy demand growing strongly in these two 
countries. Furthermore, the report states that thes e developments are contributing to a big 
improvement in their quality of life, a legitimate aspiration that needs to be accommodated 
and supported by the rest of the world. 
(b) While recognizing that enhancing energy supply and access is a key component of 
energy strategy of the country, efforts are also a foot to promote Demand Side Management 
and efficient means of power generation. Another publication of International Energy Agency, 
'Key World Energy Statistics'-2007, has estimated that per capita carbon di-oxide emission 
in India at 1.05 ton is amongst the lowest in the w orld. In comparison, per capita carbon 
emission by USA has been 19.61 tons and that of China has been 3.88 tons. Similarly, energy 
intensity expressed in terms of ratio of total prim ary energy supply to Gross Domestic 
Product (calculated on the basis of purchasing powe r parity in USS terms) has been 
comparable to standards achieved by the developed c ountries. Nevertheless, inter-alia 
following steps have been taken for development of clean and efficient energy sources: 
• Enactment of Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and establishment of the Bureau of the 
Energy Efficiency. 

144    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
• Energy efficiency/Energy conservation related measures have been taken up in a big 
way. Energy labeling programme for major energy con suming equipment has been 
launched as a consumer guide and encouragement to e nergy efficient equipment 
manufacturers. An Energy Conservation Building Code has also been launched recently 
in May, 2007 to promote energy efficient designs and architecture of new buildings. 
These would lead to effective Demand Side Management. 
• Promotion of Supercritical units for thermal generation. These are a prerequisites for 
Ultra Mega Power Plants. 
• The Electricity Act, 2003 requires that distribution companies must buy part of their 
electricity purchase from renewable sources. 
• As on 31.10.2007, out of 1,36,902 MW instal led capacity in the country, 10,175 MW 
(7.4%) is contributed by renewable. 
• In addition, highest priority has been accorded to development of hydro potential in 
the country and as on 31.10.2007 hydro capacity was 34,390 MW (25%). Hydro Power 
Initiative of 50,000 MW was launched in 2003 by the Ministry of Power to accelerate 
hydro power development. 
• India has taken a major lead in participating in th e Clean Development Mechanism 
(CDM) programme. 
• India is an active member of the Carbon Sequestration Leadership Forum. 
• India is a partner in the future Gen Project of the United States to develop an emission 
free coal fired power plan. 
T&D losses 
1419.   SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN: 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) the national average Transmission and Distribution (T&D) losses during last three 
years; 
(b) the targeted national average for T&D losses; 
(c) the time-frame set for achieving the same; 
(d) the amount of power loss in mega watts due to higher T&D losses; and 
(e) whether future power demand projection is based on present T&D losses or the 
targeted one? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) In the earlier system 
of monitoring, utilities used a monitor Transmission and Distribution (T&D) losses. In that 
system, there was a tendency of utilities booking s ubsidized/un-metered supply under 
distribution losses. T&D losses were being computed  taking into account electricity bills 
issued to consumers as accrued income and not on ac tual collection basis. T&D losses for 
the country for 2003-04,2004-05 and 2005-06 were 32.53%, 31.25% and 30.42% respectively. 
Concept of Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses was introduced in 

Written Answers to  [3 DEC. 2007]  Unstarred Questions    145 
2001-02. AT&C loss parameters capture total perform ance of the Utility. On the basis of 
available information, the Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) Loss of the State 
Power Utilities at the national level for 2003-04,2004-05 and 2005-06 was 34.90%, 34.33% 
and 34.54% respectively. 
(b) and (c) The Central Government has built a nati onal consensus to focus on a time 
bound programme for reduction of Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses. In 
the Chief Ministers' Conference held under the chai rmanship of the Prime Minister on 
28th May 2007, a unanimous resolution was adopted which inter alia included the commitment 
of the States, with appropriate assistance from the Centre, to establish the necessary baseline 
data and information technology applications for en ergy accounting and auditing, and for 
ensuring a resolute elimination of electricity theft. In the Conference, the States committed 
themselves to achieve and sustain reduction in the overall AT&C losses in the next five 
years.

11421. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a) the funds earmarked for the development, maintenance, etc. of the power sector in the 
country during the Eleventh Five Year Plan; 
(b) the target set for setting-up of new power plants in the country during this period and 
to enhance their capacity and production; 
(c) whether Government proposes to set-up an independent National Energy Fund;

(e) the positive steps Government is taking to improve power distribution system and to 
stop pilferage of electricity, so that power supply can be ensured?

Group on Power for the Eleventh Plan (2007-12) based on certain assumptions, has estimated 
a total fund requirement of about Rs. 10,31,600 crores for the power sector as a whole, which 
includes generation projects, transmission projects and distribution including rural 
electrification, human resource development, R&D etc. A capacity addition of 78,577 MW 
has been proposed for 11* Plan. According to information received from Planning 
Commission, the 11* Plan capacity addition target and outlay have not been finalized by it

Committee on the Integrated Energy Policy inter-alia recommended that National Energy 
Fund (NEF) should be set up to finance energy Research and Development (R&D).  
(e) Electricity is a concurrent subject and the responsibility of distribution segment rests 
with the States. However, Central Government has launched Accelerated Power Development 
and Reforms Programme in the year 2002-03 in order to reduce aggregate technical and 
commercial losses, improving quality of supply of power, increasing revenue collection and 
improving consumer satisfaction. Under the investment component of APDRP, financial 
assistance was given to the States as additional central assistance over and above the 
normal central plan allocation, for strengthening and upgradation of sub-transmission and 
distribution system. Furthermore, to enable effective control on theft of electricity, the 
Electricity Act, 2003 has incorporated specific provisions for detection of theft, speedy trial 
of theft related offences and also for recovery of charges of electricity stolen. Theft of 
electricity has been explicitly made a congnizable offence. The distribution licensees have 
been empowered to disconnect the supply of electricity upon detection of theft. The penalty 
for repeated theft of electricity by large consumers has also been enhanced.

Activities of PGCIL  
1426. SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that the Power Grid Corporation Limited (PGCIL) is investing a large 
amount in sectors other than power distribution; 
(b) if so, the complete details in this regard; 
(c) what are the plans of PGCIL in distribution of power during the next two years; and 
(d) whether PGCIL intends to capture foreign market in near future and if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) The Power Grid 
Corporation of India Ltd. (PGCIL) has been notified as the Central Transmission Utility (CTU) of 
India, under the Electricity Act, 2003. It undertakes the development of inter-State transmission systems 
at Extra High Voltage (EHV) level. Besides its core business of power transmission, PGCIL has also 
diversifed into the Telecom business, leveraging it s country wide power transmission 
infrastructure. The Government of India has approved an investment of about Rs. 934 crore for this 
activity. Most of the telecom network has already been installed and connectivity has been provided 
to all metros and major cities.  
During the Xth Plan, out of a total investment of about Rs. 18,919 crore, the investment in the 
telecom business was 3.5% (about Rs. 663 crore) and in the current year i.e. 2007-08, investment in the 
telecom business is envisaged to be only Rs. 11 crore (0.17% of the total budgetary outlay of Rs. 
6504 crore).  
(c) The PGCIL is entrusted with the responsibility of development of inter-State Transmission 
systems. The PGCIL plans to implement about 12,580 ckt. Kms inter-state transmission network 
during 2007-08 and 2008-09 with an investment of around Rs. 14,544 crores.  
(d) The PGCIL has secured consultancy in the area of power transmission in Bhutan, Nepal, 
Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Dubai.

Standardization of equipments for thermal power plants 
1430.   SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN: 
SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE: 
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether standardization of equipments for thermal p ower plants, including those 
having supercritical technology is being done through Central Electricity Authority (CEA), 
to ensure timely availability of spare parts at red uced cost as well as to facilitate proper 
maintenance management; and 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor? 

160    Written Answers to  [R AJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): (a) and (b) As part of various 
efforts being made to expedite execution of thermal power projects, standardization of equipment is 
being encouraged. Standardization is expected to lead to uniform design practices by various utilities 
and facilitate bulk manufacture by the equipment manufacturers, reducing project execution time and 
cost. This would also standardize spares requirements and could lead to more optimal inventory and 
maintenance management.  
However, design of thermal power plants is largely governed by site specific factors including 
plant capacity and unit configuration, location (pit head, load center, coastal), green field or 
expansion project, coal quality, water quality and soil properties. These factors make 
standardization difficult especially for balance of plant.  
Standard specifications for main plant equipment (boiler, turbine and generator) for 500 
MW+20% (500 to 600 MW) unit size are under development by CEA in consultation with utilities 
and manufacturers. As the supercritical technology is presently under introduction in the country, 
standardization of this technology is considered premature at this stage.

†1460. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV: Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that transfer of ST land to no n-scheduled tribe people has been 
banned in the country; 
(b) if so, whether Government is going to take any action to implement these provisions 
more strictly; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that Government is going to implement any stringent Saw to 
return schedule tribes' land to them which they lost for any reason and the land is with .ion 
tribal people; and 
(d) if so, the details therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI P. R. KYNDIAH): (a) to (d) The Governors  
in respect of States having Fifth Scheduled Areas therein can make regulations to prohibit 
or restrict the transfer of land by or among member s of the Scheduled Tribes in such area 
after adopting the procedure prescribed in the Fifth Scheduled to the Constitution of India. 
The States Governments have in general accepted the policy of prohibiting of transfer of 
land from tribals to non-tribals and restoration of alienated tribal lands to them and especially 
the States with large tribal population have since enacted laws for this purpose. 
Since "Land" and its management fall under the exclusive legislative and administrative 
jurisdiction of States as provided in Entry No. 18 of List-II (State List) of the Seventh 
Scheduled to the Constitution of India, the initiative have essentially to come from the State 
Governments. At the Central Government, the Ministr y of Rural Development, has been 
playing an advisory and coordinatory role in the field of land reforms.

in family based income generating activities and th e infrastructure incidental thereto. The 
objective of the scheme is to boost the demand-based income generating programme meant 
for raising the economic and social status of triba ls. National Scheduled Tribes Finance 
Development Corporation (NSTFDC) provides concessio nal financial assistance to 
Scheduled Tribes having annual family income upto double the poverty line income limit for 
undertaking self employment ventures/activities. 
Besides, the Ministry of Rural Development is also implementing poverty alleviation 
programmes such as Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) to provide wage employment 
and Sawarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) to provide self-employment to the rural 
poor. A Rural Housing Programme under the name Indira Awas Yojana (IAY) is also being 
implemented throughout the country to provide shelter to the rural people living Below the 
Poverty Line (BPL). All these programmes have special provisions for the tribal population.

Statement  
Detail regarding steps being taken to reduce violence/atrocities on women and  
children  
Law and order and other criminal matters is a State  subject under the Constitution and 
therefore, the direct responsibility for dealing wi th enforcement of the concerned Acts is 
that of the State Governments and the mechanisms under them. The registration, investigation, 
detection and prevention of crimes against, women i s primarily the responsibility of the 
State Governments/UT Administrations. However, the Government of India has initiated a 
number of measures to check such crimes, such as: 
* Enacted the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 which provides 
for more effective protection of the Constitutional rights of women, who are victims 
of violence of any kind occurring within the family including any unlawful demand 
for dowry. 
* setting up of helplines for women in distress under the Swadhar Scheme 
* support services to victims of violence through schemes such as Short Stay Homes 
and Swadhar under which shelter, maintenance, couns eling, capacity building, 
occupational training, medical aid and other services are provided 
* .grant-in-aid schemes providing assistance for rescue and rehabilitation of trafficked 
victims as well as prevention through special schemes in source areas of trafficking 
* redressal of grievances through interventions of Na tional and State Commissions 
for Women 
* organizing legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Camps 
* implementation of schemes for (i) awareness generat ion and advocacy and (ii) 
economic empowerment of women through the programme s of Rashtriya Mahila 
Kosh, Swashakti Project, Swayamsidha Project, Swawlamban Programme and Support 
to Training & Employment Programme (STEP) 
* review of laws with a view to remove provisions whi ch may be discriminatory to 
women and to enhance punishments for crimes against women 
* sensitisation of judiciary and police and civil administration on gender issues 
* Follow up of reports of cases of atrocities against  women received from various 
sources, including NCW, with concerned authorities in the Central and the State 
Governments. 

190    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
Apart from legislative changes in the relevant Acts , instructions/guidelines have been 
issued to the State Governments/Union Territory Adm inistration to effectively enforce 
legislation relating to crimes against women and monitor the enforcement and to give more 
focused attention to improving the administration o f criminal justice system and to take 
such measures as are necessary for the prevention o f crime against women and other 
vulnerable sections of society. The measures suggested include: 
* sensitizing of police officials charged with the responsibility of protecting the women 
* vigorously enforce the existing legislation relating to dowry violence 
* set up women police cells in police stations and exclusive women police stations 
* provide institutional support to the victims of violence 
* provide counseling to victims of rape 
* take measures to eliminate trafficking in women. States have also been advised to 
constitute State Advisory Committees to advise to trafficking matters 
* ensure wider recruitment of women police officers 
* train police personnel in special laws dealing with atrocities against women 
* setting up of Fast Track Courts 
* setting up of Family Courts 
* appointment of Dowry Prohibition Officers and notification of Rules under the 
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD:

Kishori Shakti Yojana 
1472.    PROF. ALKA BALRAM KSHATRIYA: 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has redesigned the already existing Adolescent Girls Scheme 
as the Kishori Shakti Yojana, seeking to significan tly expand the coverage of the 
existing scheme for adolescent girls in the age group of 11 to 18 years; 
(b) whether the KSY scheme would be using the infrastru cture of Integrated Child 
Development Scheme, since the earlier scheme was al ready a component of the 
centrally sponsored ICDS scheme; 
(c) what are the other main features of the revamped KSY scheme; and 
(d) to what extent this new Scheme has helped in achieving its aims and objectives? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD  
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) Yes, Sir. In the year 2000, the 
Ministry redesigned the erstwhile existing Adolesce nt Girls scheme and renamed it as 
Kishori Shakti Yojana (KSY) to cover adolescent girls in the age group of 11-18 years and 
the scheme was expanded to cover 2000 ICDS Projects. In 2005-06, the scheme was further 
expanded to cover 6118 ICDS Projects across the country. 
(b) Yes, Sir. KSY is being implemented using the in frastructure of Integrated child 
Development Scheme.

nutrition and family care, learning life skills, he lping them gain a better understanding of

Anomalies in adoption of children 
1473. SHRI NARESH GUJRAL: Will Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMET 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that despite India being a sec ular country, we have different 
yardsticks for different religions as far as adoption of children is concerned, in as much as 
hindus can adopt a child under Hindu Adoption Act; Christians, Muslims and others can 
only be given guardianship and not be called parents under the present law; and 
(b) what steps Government is considering to remove these anomalies? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) As per the Juvenile 
Justice (Care and protection of Children) Amendment  Act, 2006 there is no restriction in 
adoption on account of sex or religion of the child or prospective adoptive parents. 
Amendments to dowry laws 
† 1474. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN TIWARI: 
SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there are many complaints with regard to use of dowry laws for 
seeking revenge; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that many innocent persons are punished as a result thereof, 
while culprits get scot free; 
(c) if so, whether Government would consider to make amendments in the provisions of 
the dowry law, to prevent its misuse and for punishing the culprits; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) As per the data compiled 
by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), Ministry of Home Affairs, for the period 
2004-2006, out of the 11300 cases registered under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, 615 
were declared false on account of mistake of fact or law. 
(c) Penal provisions already exist in the Dowry Prohibtion Act, 1961 in respect of offences 
under the Act. Government has no proposal to amend the Act in order to prevent its alleged 
misuse. 
(d) Does not arise.
